disagreements.topic: Realized copper deck for the horizon-date NTM (range $5.85-6.05/lb)
disagreements.positions: Agents 1 and 4 use $5.85/lb, agent 2 $5.90, agent 5 $6.00 and agent 3 $6.05. All five sit below the round-1 supervisor's $6.00 or near it, and all argue that realized prices run below LME.
disagreements.resolution: Settled: the range is consistent with the data. Ero's realized price runs ~4-5% below LME cash. Q2-26 realized was $5.78 against an LME average of $13,324/t ($6.04/lb), and H1 realized was $5.65 against an LME average of $13,088/t ($5.94/lb). The agents' $5.85-6.05 therefore implies LME of ~$6.13-6.34/lb (~$13,500-14,000/t), in line with Goldman's $13,800/t for 2027 and ~5-7% below September spot ($14,480/t). At spot, realized would be ~$6.27. The deck prices in a moderate mean reversion that sits inside the bank range, so no correction is needed. Q3-26 realized should come in near $6.1/lb (Jul-Sep LME average ~$14,120/t), which supports faster H2-26 deleveraging.
disagreements.evidence: Ero Q2-26 MD&A (realized $5.78 Q2, $5.65 YTD); Westmetall LME cash-settlement monthly averages for 2026.

disagreements.positions: Agents 2 and 3 (following the round-1 supervisor) say $23 is ~3.7-3.8x 2027 EBITDA at $5.00 copper. Agents 1, 4 and 5 recompute it at ~4.9-5.2x. The levels are $22 (agent 2) and $23 (agents 1, 3, 4 and 5).
disagreements.resolution: Settled: 3.8x was an arithmetic error. At $23, equity is $2.44B (106M shares) and EV is ~$2.65-2.75B. Against ~$520-560M of EBITDA at $5.00 copper, that is ~4.8-5.2x; the ~3.8x multiple applies only at the base deck (~$690-710M). $23 is still a sensible break, because trading there needs copper below every bank 2027 forecast or an operating failure. The multiple is just less extreme than the round-1 note said.
disagreements.evidence: Arithmetic from Q2-26 MD&A share count (105.88M diluted) and the agents' own $5.00-deck EBITDA builds.

disagreements.topic: 2027 copper C1 cost ($2.25-2.28 in all agents)
disagreements.positions: All agents use C1 of $2.25-2.28/lb for NTM at the horizon, in the middle of 2026 guidance.
disagreements.resolution: Left unchanged, flagged as a mild downside risk. YTD 2026 C1 is $2.40/lb (Q1 $2.39, Q2 $2.42), above the top of 2026 guidance ($2.15-2.35). Higher 2027-28 volume and the BRL collars (floor 5.40) through Dec-2027 argue for some improvement, but no 2027 cost guidance exists. Each +$0.10/lb of C1 costs ~$17-18M of EBITDA, about -$1/share at 6x. This is a risk to watch at the February 2027 guidance, not a correctable error.
disagreements.evidence: Ero Q2-26 MD&A (C1 table and 2026 guidance).

disagreements.topic: Xavantina gold volume in the NTM EBITDA (agents assume ~55koz mined at a $2,200-2,700/oz margin, ~$120-150M)
disagreements.positions: Agents 1-5 all take ~55koz, the midpoint of the filed 2027-28 outlook of 50-60koz.
disagreements.resolution: Consistent with the filed outlook, but it needs a steep ramp. Mined gold was 14.2koz in H1-26 (Q2 8.7koz, ~35koz/yr run-rate). 2026 mined guidance of 40-50koz was held but pointed 'to the low end' and weighted heavily to H2. Historic concentrate sales end mid-2027, so the Q4-27 to Q3-28 NTM period rests on mined ounces only. A 45koz outcome would cut ~$25M of EBITDA (~-$1.4/share). Mined-gold C1 guidance was also raised to $1,100-1,350/oz. I treat this as a mild downside risk, partly offset by gold spot (~$4,250) sitting above the agents' $3,800-4,000 deck, and I make no ladder change.
disagreements.evidence: Ero Q2-26 results release and MD&A (mined gold 8,693oz Q2, 14,188oz H1; guidance 40-50koz at the low end; updated gold C1 and AISC guidance).

disagreements.topic: Weight and level of the long-term-deck NAV leg ($26-30.5)
disagreements.positions: Agents 1 and 3 have NAV at ~$26 (1.0x, $5.00 long-term Cu), agent 2 a DCF of $30, agent 4 $30.5 (at $4.75 long-term) and agent 5 $29 at a 10% weight. The others weight it at 20%. It is the main reason the mean fair value ($35.8) sits below the mean ladder median (~$36.8) and spot ($37.87).
disagreements.resolution: Not settled by search; there is no primary NAV to check against. The spread comes from mine-life and sustaining-capex assumptions, not from a factual error. Agent 4 at $4.75 long-term gets a higher NAV than agents 1 and 3 at $5.00, which points to longer mine lives. The weights (10-20%) are reasonable. I leave the blend at the mean.
disagreements.evidence: Agents' method inputs; peer P/NAV range 0.82-0.95x (Skillings, May 2026, as in round 1).

disagreements.topic: Guidance and catalyst facts after the Sept-14 Capital Markets Day
disagreements.positions: All agents now use the filed outlook (75-85kt for 2027, 80-90kt for 2028) with Pilar operational in 2027, and Q3 results in early November.
disagreements.resolution: Confirmed. The company describes the Pilar external shaft handover as 'expected in 2027', and the Furnas PFS is targeted for publication in 2027. No Q3-26 results date has been announced yet, and no guidance change has been filed.
disagreements.evidence: Feb-5-2026 outlook release; CMD announcement 6-K (2026-09-01); search for a Q3 release-date announcement returned none.

confidence_reason: The revised forecasts converge tightly: fair values $35.2-36.5, medians ~$36.5-37, and P(>=38) of 0.46-0.48 across all five. My searches confirmed their copper deck, share count, net debt path and guidance, and found no material error. The two new points roughly cancel: C1 running at $2.40 YTD and slow mined-gold ramp on the downside, strong Q3-26 realized copper and deleveraging on the upside. I therefore keep the mean ladder unchanged. The only corrections are to the thesis-break reasoning and a small rounding of the thesis-break level.
thesis_break_reason: At $23, equity is ~$2.44B and EV ~$2.65-2.75B with $200-300M net debt. That is ~4.8-5.2x 2027 EBITDA at $5.00/lb copper (not ~3.8x, as the round-1 note said) and ~3.8x the base-deck NTM EBITDA of ~$700M. Reaching it needs copper sustained below ~$5/lb, which is under every current bank 2027 forecast (Citi ~$5.44, Goldman ~$6.26), or a company-specific failure: Pilar shaft handover slipping past 2027, Tucuma filtration not lifting throughput, 2027 guidance (Feb-2027) well below the 75-85kt outlook, or C1 staying at or above $2.40 with the mined-gold ramp stalling.
key_drivers: Copper: LME cash averaged $14,480/t (~$6.57/lb) in September 2026. Ero realizes ~4-5% below LME (Q2-26: $5.78 vs $6.04), so the agents' $5.85-6.05 realized deck implies ~$13,500-14,000/t LME, in line with Goldman's 2027 view. Each $0.50/lb is ~$85-90M of EBITDA, about $4-5/share at 6x.
Volume step-up per the filed outlook: 75-85kt Cu in 2027 and 80-90kt in 2028, dependent on the Pilar shaft handover in 2027. H1-26 copper output was 34.6kt, against 2026 guidance of 67.5-77.5kt.
Costs: C1 is running at $2.40/lb YTD, above 2026 guidance of $2.15-2.35, while agents use $2.25 for 2027. BRL collars ($450M, floor 5.40) run through Dec-2027.
Xavantina: mined gold is running at ~35koz/yr (Q2-26 8.7koz), against the 50-60koz 2027-28 outlook the agents' ~$130M gold EBITDA relies on. Historic concentrate sales end mid-2027.

Deleveraging: net debt was $452.7M at Q2-26 (leverage 0.8x), with capex peaking in 2026 and Q3 realized copper near $6.1. Horizon net debt of ~$100-200M and the start of capital returns underpin the base case.

fair_value.reason: I keep the mean of the revised forecasters. The agents now agree on 106M diluted shares, $150-175M horizon net debt, a $5.85-6.05 realized copper deck (checked against the ~4.5% realized-to-LME discount), Furnas on a 60% attributable risked basis (~$0.4B), and bottom-up EPS of ~$3.6-3.9. The blend is ~$37-38 on EV/EBITDA and P/E, with a 10-20% long-term-deck NAV leg at $26-30.5. My new points roughly offset: a mined-gold shortfall to ~45-50koz (-$0.7 to -1.4) and C1 risk against Q3-26 realized copper near $6.1 plus faster H2-26 deleveraging (+$0.5 to +1). So I make no change.

changes.why: Four of five agents are at $23; at $23 the EV is already ~4.8-5.2x EBITDA at $5.00 copper, a level that needs copper below every bank 2027 forecast or an operating failure, so agent 2's $22 is not needed.

changes.item: Fact: EV/EBITDA at $23 with $5.00 copper (round-1 supervisor, repeated by agents 2 and 3)
changes.why: EV of $2.44B equity plus ~$0.25B net debt, divided by ~$520-560M of EBITDA at $5.00 copper, is ~4.8-5.2x; 3.8x was an arithmetic error that applies only at the base deck.

summary: After round two the five forecasts agree closely: fair value $35.2-36.5 (mean $35.8), median ~$37 and P(>=38) ~0.47, against a $37.87 close. My checks confirm their inputs. Ero realizes ~4.5% below LME, so the $5.85-6.05 deck matches Goldman's 2027 view; net debt was $452.7M and falling; 106M shares; and the 75-85kt / 80-90kt outlook still stands. Two quiet risks roughly offset the stronger Q3 copper price: C1 is running at $2.40, above guidance, and mined gold is only ~35koz/yr against the 50-60koz the models assume. I keep the mean ladder with low confidence and correct only the thesis-break reasoning ($23 is ~5x EBITDA at $5 copper, not ~3.8x), leaving the break at $23.

sizing.entry: 2 tranches: half now, half after the Brazil runoff (Oct 25) and Q3-26 results (early November, date not yet announced), which will show H2 C1 and mined-gold progress
sizing.overlap: Little direct overlap. GOOGL and META (AI data-center and grid capex) and TSLA (EVs) are indirect copper-demand drivers, so a risk-off move or an AI-capex slowdown would hit them together with ERO.
sizing.reason: Consensus fair value (~$36) is slightly below the $37.87 price, so there is no valuation edge. The stock is a ~2x-levered copper bet at record prices, with 50%+ volatility, single-country Brazil exposure and single-shaft execution risk. A ~4% cap (~$1,350 of $33,861) limits a fall to the $23 break to ~1.6% of the portfolio while adding a real-asset diversifier to a tech-heavy book. Liquidity is fine: it is a seasoned NYSE/TSX listing.
